title: How a QR code still scans when it's torn or smudged
description: QR codes hold extra backup data, so a damaged code can often still be read. Here's how that works.

scenes.big: Why damaged QR codes still scan
scenes.sub: a ripped one can still work
scenes.say: Ever scanned a QR code that was scratched or half covered, and it still worked? That's not luck. It's built in.
A QR code stores extra error-correcting data alongside your message. You pick a level when you make one. Low recovers about seven percent of damage. High recovers about thirty percent.
The scanner uses that backup to rebuild what's missing, using math rather than guesswork. It's like a sentence that still makes sense with a few letters smudged.
Those three big squares in the corners have a special ratio of black and white, one, one, three, one, one. Designers chose it because it rarely appears in print, so scanners spot it from any angle.
